composers_checked.name: Haydn, Joseph
composers_checked.note: String trios (Hob. V) complete against the Wikipedia work list and the Wiener Philharmonia Trio's 34-trio complete recording; Hob. II:2 string quintet added from the gap check

note:
Haydn, string trios: complete. Kept the 18 surviving trios of Hob. V (V:1-21 less the lost V:5, 9, 14; Henle prints them in two volumes after the Haydn complete edition) and the recorded lettered trios. Floor from the Wiener Philharmonia Trio's complete recording on Camerata Tokyo (34 trios, CMCD-10002, 2009; vols. 1-4 on Apple Music with timings, the full disc list on netoff.co.jp), with Camerata Berolinensis (Musikmanufaktur), The Vivaldi Project and the Gaede Trio (TACET) for some works; minutes = median of the recordings' timings, null where only the disc list was seen (vols. 5-6).
(1) Gap additions, imslpPage null: Hob. V:D3, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, G4 and A2 (Robbins Landon's Doblinger numbering, Nos. 20 and 25-34 in the Camerata set), all of unproven authorship and known only from that recording; confidence low where I saw no track timings. The owner may prefer to keep only the 18 numbered trios: then drop the lettered ones (D1, G1, F1, B1, G3 and the eight gap works).
(2) Outside my formation: the Divertimento (Cassatio) a cinque in G, Hob. II:2 (1753-54, 2 violins, 2 violas, basso), which c22 flagged because no Haydn slice covers string quintets. The BIS booklet (BIS-CD-1806/08) names one player per part and calls it a 'string quintet'; added with gap true, formation string-quintet. Basso given as cello (the BIS personnel list has a cellist and a double bassist for the set).
(3) Overlap with c24: its input has '6 Trios, Op.3 (Haydn, Joseph)' (Longman 1778, 2 violins and continuo), which holds Hob. V:F1, 19, D2, 18, 15 and 16, the works kept here from their own pages. c24 should skip that page as a duplicate, not keep it as continuo trio sonatas; Haydn's trios have a plain cello bass (Henle: 2 violins and cello). Likewise the Op. 38 trios Hob. IV:6-11 (flute or violin, violin, cello) are c24's, filed as winds-strings.
(4) The Cassations Hob. II:21 and II:22 (2 horns and strings, one to a part) are in my outOfScope list as 'string orchestra'; they are wind-and-string sextets for c24, not added here (c22 made the same point).
(5) Authenticity: IMSLP's Op. 8 page quotes Grove calling V:3 and V:4 doubtful in the Haydn-Werke and V:17 and V:20 'probably not authentic'; Henle and every recording include them among the authentic trios, so they are kept without a note. Wikipedia marks D2, G2, G3 and A1 doubtful: D2, G2 and A1 are unrecorded and skipped; G3 is recorded and kept with a note. G2 and A1 may be Michael Haydn's (Hummel's Op. 8 prints his MH 6 in G and MH 8 in A as Nos. 5-6).
(6) IMSLP data: the page 'String Trio in C major, Hob.V:16' gives 'V:17' in its catalogue field; Camerata Berolinensis's Vol. 1 labels V:21 'Hob. V:3' (the Adagio siciliano identifies it).
(7) Levels: all 3 on the Op. 1 quartet benchmark (3); the graders should look at the trios with long Adagio cantabile movements (V:4, 10, 12). floor.published left blank: I opened no publisher page (Henle's Urtext volumes and Doblinger's Diletto musicale editions exist per search results).
(8) Arrangements skipped: Op. 53 (André, after Hob. XVI:40-42), Gárdonyi's baryton-trio versions, the viola d'amore pastiche and the 12 German Dances; the 3 trios for three violins (outOfScope) are also arrangements.
